note:
FIRST measurement of the path production actually reads. routes/chat.js:587 sends the turn through Brain.assembleContext with PIC as the FLOOR, and AQUA_CONTEXT_V2=on ships in the environment template — so retrieval-core.v1 has been grading an intermediate stage the Context Engine overrides before anything reaches the model.

THE CONTEXT ENGINE IS CURRENTLY WORSE THAN THE FLOOR IT WRAPS. Same world, same 200 queries, same shared scorer (retrievalScoring.mjs); the only variable is which function is asked:
  recall_at_8        0.7560 -> 0.6786   (-0.077)
  mrr                0.6865 -> 0.6448
  ndcg_at_8          0.6710 -> 0.6151
  top1_kind          0.5714 -> 0.5298
  recall_direct      1.0000 -> 0.9636   (it loses answers on the EASIEST category)
  recall_superseded  0.6000 -> 0.3000   (halved)
  recall_temporal    0.6800 -> 0.5600
  recall_negation    0.8000 -> 0.7000
It buys 3 fewer noise lines (16 -> 13) at that price. unknown_honesty is unchanged.

CAUSE, TRACED: the assembler rescores the floor's pool on ten dimensions, and the floor's own relevance score — the factAffinity number that knows what the question ASKED — is not one of them and is not passed in. gatherCandidates drops it, along with entityIds and timestamp. So the layer that decides what reaches the model ranks on ten importance signals and zero relevance signals. That is the same defect the PIC gate was built to close one layer down ('an expression in which the QUESTION does not appear'), reproduced above it.

13 of 168 answerable queries lose their answer entirely to this. A fix must raise these toward the floor WITHOUT giving back noise_lines or unknown_honesty. Beating the floor is the actual target — a Context Engine that merely matches it is not earning its place on the turn path.

Regenerate with: npm run eval:gate -- context-core --update
